narration: This week's parsha is Parshas Bereishis!
In the beginning, there was nothing at all. Then Hashem created the whole world.
On the first day, Hashem said: Let there be light! And there was light.
On the second day, Hashem made the sky. On the third day, He gathered the waters into seas, and dry land appeared, full of grass and trees.
On the fourth day, Hashem made the sun, the moon and the stars.
At first, the sun and the moon were the same size. But the moon complained, so Hashem made it smaller,
and to make the moon feel better, Hashem gave it the stars to keep it company.
On the fifth day came the fish and the birds, and on the sixth day, all the animals.
Then Hashem made the very first person: Adam.
Hashem brought all the animals to Adam, and Adam gave each one its name.
The plants had been waiting just under the ground. When Adam saw that they needed rain, he davened, and the rain came, and everything began to grow!
On the seventh day, Hashem rested, and made the day holy. It was the very first Shabbos.
The world was beautiful, but something was still missing. Then Shabbos came, and with it came rest.
Hashem planted a beautiful garden, Gan Eden, and put Adam there to take care of it.
Hashem said: You may eat from every tree, except one, the Eitz HaDaas, the Tree of Knowledge.
Then Hashem made Chava, the first woman, to be Adam's wife.
But the nachash, the snake, was very clever, and very sneaky.
He tricked Chava into eating from the tree, and Chava gave some to Adam too.
Suddenly, they knew they had done something wrong.
Hashem called out to Adam: Ayeka? Where are you?
Adam and Chava had to leave Gan Eden. From now on, people would have to work hard for their food.
And to guard the way back to the Tree of Life, Hashem placed angels, and a fiery, turning sword.
Adam and Chava had two sons, Kayin and Hevel. Kayin was a farmer, and Hevel was a shepherd.
Kayin brought Hashem a korban from his worst fruits. Hevel brought the very best of his sheep.
A fire came down from heaven and took Hevel's korban, but not Kayin's.
Kayin became so jealous and angry that he killed his brother Hevel.
Hashem punished Kayin, and he had to wander from place to place.
Adam and Chava had another son, Shes. Many generations passed, and people lived for hundreds of years.
Adam lived nine hundred and thirty years, and Mesushelach lived longest of all: nine hundred and sixty-nine years!
There was Chanoch, a tzaddik. Hashem took him from the world early, so that he would always stay good.
But as the years went by, people stopped listening to Hashem, and the world filled with wrongdoing.
Hashem was sad, and decided that the world could not go on like this.
But one man found favor in Hashem's eyes. His name was Noach.
And that's a story for next week!
Good Shabbos!
